cases.reason: Asked when the Sony is back in stock, the model on the MCP path calls get_warehouse_availability, not get_restock_schedule (accuracy 0.00 against 1.00). The MCP restock tool has a different description and result shape (see parity). One recorded model choice; whether the swap alone causes it is not shown. Left open in #303.
Both paths score 0.50 and neither calls compare_products; the MCP recording searches a third time. A recorded model choice, no accuracy difference.
The native recording also calls recall_memories (a local tool both paths offer); the MCP recording goes straight to semantic_search. Accuracy is 1.00 on both.

parity.reason: The native tool also returns image_url and on_sale per product.
The native tool also returns in_stock, on_sale, seller and total_stock.
The native tool also returns in_stock and original_price per product.
The native tool also returns a trend summary.
The native tool returns an object (product, upcoming_restocks, next_restock); the MCP tool returns the bare list of restocks.
Different field names and nesting (options and shipping_options, destination and destination_region, ships_from as an object or a string).
The native tool returns an object with carriers, best_value and fastest; the MCP tool returns the bare list with estimated_days as a string.

Different ranking: the native tool orders by units sold, the MCP tool by order count, so the top five differ. The fields differ too (units_sold and order_count against recent_orders and review_count).
